claims.text: Arc melting on a water-cooled copper hearth provides rapid quenching of the FeCoNi-based alloy.
Rapid quenching will trap a metastable microstructure.
Rapid quenching will increase grain-boundary density.
Rapid quenching will promote or retain phase separation.
Increased grain-boundary density and phase separation will increase the number of magnetic-domain pinning sites.
A greater density of magnetic-domain pinning sites will increase coercivity.
Related FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives have soft-ferromagnetic properties.
A qualifying composition must be nearly equiatomic and have configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Rapid quenching will produce a refined grain structure with more grain boundaries.
Rapid quenching may stabilize metastable phases.
Rapid quenching limits the time available for atomic diffusion.
Limited atomic diffusion produces a more homogeneous microstructure.
Limited atomic diffusion produces a finely grained microstructure.
Defects and grain boundaries act as domain-wall pinning sites.
Rapidly quenched samples will have higher coercivity than composition-matched, slowly cooled samples.
Inadequate quenching or deviations from equiatomic composition may prevent the predicted microstructural and coercivity enhancements.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement depends on the extent of grain refinement and phase stabilization.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says rapid quenching will trap phase separation, whereas the mechanism says limited diffusion will create a more homogeneous microstructure. The relevant length scales or meanings of homogeneity and phase separation are not distinguished.
